NASB.1: Then it came about, when Jabin king of Hazor heard [of it], that he sent to Jobab king of Madon and to the king of Shimron and to the king of Achshaph,
NASB.2: and to the kings who were of the north in the hill country, and in the Arabah-- south of Chinneroth and in the lowland and on the heights of Dor on the west--
NASB.3: to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, and the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpeh.
NASB.4: They came out, they and all their armies with them, [as] many people as the sand that is on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
NASB.5: So all of these kings having agreed to meet, came and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight against Israel.
NASB.6: Then the LORD said to Joshua, 'Do not be afraid because of them, for tomorrow at this time I will deliver all of them slain before Israel; you shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.'
NASB.7: So Joshua and all the people of war with him came upon them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and attacked them.
NASB.8: The LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, so that they defeated them, and pursued them as far as Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim and the valley of Mizpeh to the east; and they struck them until no survivor was left to them.
NASB.9: Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him; he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
NASB.10: Then Joshua turned back at that time, and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword; for Hazor formerly was the head of all these kingdoms.
NASB.11: They struck every person who was in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying [them]; there was no one left who breathed. And he burned Hazor with fire.
NASB.12: Joshua captured all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, [and] utterly destroyed them; just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
NASB.13: However, Israel did not burn any cities that stood on their mounds, except Hazor alone, [which] Joshua burned.
NASB.14: All the spoil of these cities and the cattle, the sons of Israel took as their plunder; but they struck every man with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them. They left no one who breathed.
NASB.15: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did; he left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.16: Thus Joshua took all that land: the hill country and all the Negev, all that land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its lowland
NASB.17: from Mount Halak, that rises toward Seir, even as far as Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon at the foot of Mount Hermon. And he captured all their kings and struck them down and put them to death.
NASB.18: Joshua waged war a long time with all these kings.
NASB.19: There was not a city which made peace with the sons of Israel except the Hivites living in Gibeon; they took them all in battle.
NASB.20: For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts, to meet Israel in battle in order that he might utterly destroy them, that they might receive no mercy, but that he might destroy them, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.21: Then Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab and from all the hill country of Judah and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.
NASB.22: There were no Anakim left in the land of the sons of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod some remained.
NASB.23: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses, and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Thus the land had rest from war.

NKJV.1: And it came to pass, when Jabin king of Hazor heard these things, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
NKJV.2: and to the kings who were from the north, in the mountains, in the plain south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
NKJV.3: to the Canaanites in the east and in the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite in the mountains, and the Hivite below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
NKJV.4: So they went out, they and all their armies with them, as many people as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.
NKJV.5: And when all these kings had met together, they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
NKJV.6: But the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid because of them, for tomorrow about this time I will deliver all of them slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
NKJV.7: So Joshua and all the people of war with him came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and they attacked them.
NKJV.8: And the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, who defeated them and chased them to Greater Sidon, to the Brook Misrephoth, and to the Valley of Mizpah eastward; they attacked them until they left none of them remaining.
NKJV.9: So Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
NKJV.10: Joshua turned back at that time and took Hazor, and struck its king with the sword; for Hazor was formerly the head of all those kingdoms.
NKJV.11: And they struck all the people who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them. There was none left breathing. Then he burned Hazor with fire.
NKJV.12: So all the cities of those kings, and all their kings, Joshua took and struck with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
NKJV.13: But as for the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel burned none of them, except Hazor only, which Joshua burned.
NKJV.14: And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock, the children of Israel took as booty for themselves; but they struck every man with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, and they left none breathing.
NKJV.15: As the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
NKJV.16: Thus Joshua took all this land: the mountain country, all the South, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, and the Jordan plain—the mountains of Israel and its lowlands,
NKJV.17: from Mount Halak and the ascent to Seir, even as far as Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, and struck them down and killed them.
NKJV.18: Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
NKJV.19: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. All the others they took in battle.
NKJV.20: For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that He might utterly destroy them, and that they might receive no mercy, but that He might destroy them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NKJV.21: And at that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the mountains: from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, from all the mountains of Judah, and from all the mountains of Israel; Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.
NKJV.22: None of the Anakim were left in the land of the children of Israel; they remained only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod.
NKJV.23: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had said to Moses; and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Then the land rested from war.

ESV.1: When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard of this, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
ESV.2: and to the kings who were in the northern hill country, and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, and in the lowland, and in Naphoth-dor on the west,
ESV.3: to the Canaanites in the east and the west, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
ESV.4: And they came out with all their troops, a great horde, in number like the sand that is on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
ESV.5: And all these kings joined their forces and came and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
ESV.6: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will give over all of them, slain, to Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
ESV.7: So Joshua and all his warriors came suddenly against them by the waters of Merom and fell upon them.
ESV.8: And the LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, who struck them and chased them as far as Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and eastward as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. And they struck them until he left none remaining.
ESV.9: And Joshua did to them just as the LORD said to him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
ESV.10: And Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor formerly was the head of all those kingdoms.
ESV.11: And they struck with the sword all who were in it, devoting them to destruction;  there was none left that breathed. And he burned Hazor with fire.
ESV.12: And all the cities of those kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and struck them with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
ESV.13: But none of the cities that stood on mounds did Israel burn, except Hazor alone; that Joshua burned.
ESV.14: And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock, the people of Israel took for their plunder. But every person they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, and they did not leave any who breathed.
ESV.15: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.16: So Joshua took all that land, the hill country and all the Negeb and all the land of Goshen and the lowland and the Arabah and the hill country of Israel and its lowland
ESV.17: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. And he captured all their kings and struck them and put them to death.
ESV.18: Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
ESV.19: There was not a city that made peace with the people of Israel except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took them all in battle.
ESV.20: For it was the LORD's doing to harden their hearts that they should come against Israel in battle, in order that they should be devoted to destruction and should receive no mercy but be destroyed, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
ESV.21: And Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction with their cities.
ESV.22: There was none of the Anakim left in the land of the people of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod did some remain.
ESV.23: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses. And Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their tribal allotments. And the land had rest from war.

AMP.1: Then when Jabin king of Hazor heard [of Israel's other victories] he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
AMP.2: and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country, and in the Arabah [the plain] south of Chinnereth (the Sea of Galilee) and in the lowland and on the hills of Dor on the west;
AMP.3: to the Canaanite in the east and in the west, and to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite at the foot of [Mount] Hermon in the land of Mizpeh.
AMP.4: They went out, they and all their armies with them, as many people as the sand on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
AMP.5: So all these kings met and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight against Israel.
AMP.6: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid because of them, for tomorrow by this time I am going to hand over all of them slain [by the sword] to Israel; you shall hamstring (disable) their horses and set fire to their chariots."
AMP.7: So Joshua and all the people of war with him came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and attacked them.
AMP.8: The LORD handed them over to Israel, who struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim and eastward as far as the Valley of Mizpeh; they struck them down until no survivor was left.
AMP.9: Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him; he hamstrung (disabled) their horses and set fire to their chariots.
AMP.10: At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and struck its king dead with the sword; for Hazor previously was the head of all these kingdoms.
AMP.11: They struck all the people who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them; there was no one left who breathed. And he set fire to Hazor.
AMP.12: Joshua captured all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
AMP.13: But Israel did not burn any of the cities that stood [walled and fortified] on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.
AMP.14: The sons of Israel took as their plunder all the spoil of these cities and the cattle; but they struck every man with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them. They left no one alive.
AMP.15: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses had commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did; he left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
AMP.16: So Joshua took all this land: the hill country, all the Negev (South country), all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah [plain], the hill country of Israel and its lowland
AMP.17: from Mount Halak, that rises toward Seir [in the south], even as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon at the foot of Mount Hermon [in the north]. He captured all their kings and struck them and put them to death.
AMP.18: Joshua waged war with all these kings a long time [at least five years].
AMP.19: There was no city that made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon; they took all the others in battle.
AMP.20: For it was [the purpose] of the LORD to harden their hearts, to meet Israel in battle so that Israel would utterly destroy them, that they would receive no mercy, but that Israel would destroy them, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
AMP.21: Then Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.
AMP.22: There were no Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod [of Philistia] some remained.
AMP.23: So Joshua took the whole land [of Canaan], according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. So the land had rest from war.

CSB17.1: When King Jabin of Hazor heard this news, he sent a message to: King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
CSB17.2: and the kings of the north in the hill country, the Arabah south of Chinnereth, <sup>ⓙ</sup> the Judean foothills, <sup>[1]</sup> and the Slopes of Dor <sup>[2]</sup> to the west,
CSB17.3: the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hethites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpah. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.4: They went out with all their armies — a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore <sup>ⓛ</sup>  — along with a vast number of horses and chariots.
CSB17.5: All these kings joined forces; they came and camped together at the Waters of Merom to attack Israel. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.6: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for at this time tomorrow I will cause all of them to be killed before Israel. <sup>ⓝ</sup> You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.7: So Joshua and all his troops surprised them at the Waters of Merom and attacked them.
CSB17.8: The LORD handed them over to Israel, and they struck them down, pursuing them as far as greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and to the east as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. <sup>ⓑ</sup> They struck them down, leaving no survivors. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.9: Joshua treated them as the LORD had told him; he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots.
CSB17.10: At that time Joshua turned back, captured Hazor, and struck down its king with the sword, because Hazor had formerly been the leader of all these kingdoms.
CSB17.11: They struck down everyone in it with the sword, completely destroying <sup>ⓓ</sup> them; he left no one alive. Then he burned Hazor.
CSB17.12: Joshua captured all these kings and their cities and struck them down with the sword. He completely destroyed them, as Moses the LORD’s servant <sup>ⓔ</sup> had commanded.
CSB17.13: However, Israel did not burn any of the cities that stood on their mounds except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
CSB17.14: The Israelites plundered all the spoils and cattle of these cities for themselves. But they struck down every person with the sword until they had annihilated them, leaving no one alive.
CSB17.15: Just as the LORD had commanded his servant Moses, Moses commanded Joshua. That is what Joshua did, leaving nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
CSB17.16: So Joshua took all this land — the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, <sup>ⓕ</sup> the foothills, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its foothills —
CSB17.17: from Mount Halak, <sup>ⓖ</sup> which ascends to Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon at the foot of Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down, putting them to death. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.18: Joshua waged war with all these kings for a long time.
CSB17.19: No city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites who inhabited Gibeon; <sup>ⓘ</sup> all of them were taken in battle.
CSB17.20: For it was the LORD’s intention to harden their hearts, <sup>ⓙ</sup> so that they would engage Israel in battle, be completely destroyed without mercy, and be annihilated, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
CSB17.21: At that time Joshua proceeded to exterminate the Anakim <sup>ⓚ</sup> from the hill country — Hebron, Debir, Anab — all the hill country of Judah and of Israel. Joshua completely destroyed them with their cities.
CSB17.22: No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites, except for some remaining in Gaza, Gath, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and Ashdod.
CSB17.23: So Joshua took the entire land, in keeping with all that the LORD had told Moses. Joshua then gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their tribal allotments. After this, the land had rest from war. <sup>ⓜ</sup>

NLT.1: When King Jabin of Hazor heard what had happened, he sent messages to the following kings: King Jobab of Madon; the king of Shimron; the king of Acshaph;
NLT.2: all the kings of the northern hill country; the kings in the Jordan Valley south of Galilee ; the kings in the Galilean foothills ; the kings of Naphoth-dor on the west;
NLT.3: the kings of Canaan, both east and west; the kings of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites in the towns on the slopes of Mount Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
NLT.4: All these kings came out to fight. Their combined armies formed a vast horde. And with all their horses and chariots, they covered the landscape like the sand on the seashore.
NLT.5: The kings joined forces and established their camp around the water near Merom to fight against Israel.
NLT.6: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel as dead men. Then you must cripple their horses and burn their chariots.”
NLT.7: So Joshua and all his fighting men traveled to the water near Merom and attacked suddenly.
NLT.8: And the LORD gave them victory over their enemies. The Israelites chased them as far as Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and eastward into the valley of Mizpah, until not one enemy warrior was left alive.
NLT.9: Then Joshua crippled the horses and burned all the chariots, as the LORD had instructed.
NLT.10: Joshua then turned back and captured Hazor and killed its king. (Hazor had at one time been the capital of all these kingdoms.)
NLT.11: The Israelites completely destroyed every living thing in the city, leaving no survivors. Not a single person was spared. And then Joshua burned the city.
NLT.12: Joshua slaughtered all the other kings and their people, completely destroying them, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded.
NLT.13: But the Israelites did not burn any of the towns built on mounds except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
NLT.14: And the Israelites took all the plunder and livestock of the ravaged towns for themselves. But they killed all the people, leaving no survivors.
NLT.15: As the LORD had commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua. And Joshua did as he was told, carefully obeying all the commands that the LORD had given to Moses.
NLT.16: So Joshua conquered the entire region — the hill country, the entire Negev, the whole area around the town of Goshen, the western foothills, the Jordan Valley, the mountains of Israel, and the Galilean foothills.
NLT.17: The Israelite territory now extended all the way from Mount Halak, which leads up to Seir in the south, as far north as Baal-gad at the foot of Mount Hermon in the valley of Lebanon. Joshua killed all the kings of those territories,
NLT.18: waging war for a long time to accomplish this.
NLT.19: No one in this region made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites of Gibeon. All the others were defeated.
NLT.20: For the LORD hardened their hearts and caused them to fight the Israelites. So they were completely destroyed without mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.21: During this period Joshua destroyed all the descendants of Anak, who lived in the hill country of Hebron, Debir, Anab, and the entire hill country of Judah and Israel. He killed them all and completely destroyed their towns.
NLT.22: None of the descendants of Anak were left in all the land of Israel, though some still remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
NLT.23: So Joshua took control of the entire land, just as the LORD had instructed Moses. He gave it to the people of Israel as their special possession, dividing the land among the tribes. So the land finally had rest from war.

NET.1: When King Jabin of Hazor heard the news, he organized a coalition, including King Jobab of Madon, the king of Shimron, the king of Acshaph,
NET.2: and the northern kings who ruled in the hill country, the Arabah south of Kinnereth, the lowlands, and the heights of Dor to the west.
NET.3: Canaanites came from the east and west; Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites from the hill country; and Hivites from below Hermon in the area of Mizpah.
NET.4: These kings came out with their armies; they were as numerous as the sand on the seashore and had a large number of horses and chariots.
NET.5: All these kings gathered and joined forces at the Waters of Merom to fight Israel.
NET.6: The LORD told Joshua, “Don’t be afraid of them, for about this time tomorrow I will cause all of them to lie dead before Israel. You must hamstring their horses and burn their chariots.”
NET.7: Joshua and his whole army caught them by surprise at the Waters of Merom and attacked them.
NET.8: The LORD handed them over to Israel and they struck them down and chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, Misrephoth Maim, and the Mizpah Valley to the east. They struck them down until no survivors remained.
NET.9: Joshua did to them as the LORD had commanded him; he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots.
NET.10: At that time Joshua turned, captured Hazor, and struck down its king with the sword, for Hazor was at that time the leader of all these kingdoms.
NET.11: They annihilated everyone who lived there with the sword — no one who breathed remained — and burned Hazor.
NET.12: Joshua captured all these royal cities and all their kings and annihilated them with the sword, as Moses the LORD’s servant had commanded.
NET.13: But Israel did not burn any of the cities located on mounds, except for Hazor; it was the only one Joshua burned.
NET.14: The Israelites plundered all the goods of these cities and the cattle, but they totally destroyed all the people and allowed no one who breathed to live.
NET.15: Moses the LORD’s servant passed on the LORD’s commands to Joshua, and Joshua did as he was told. He did not ignore any of the commands the LORD had given Moses.
NET.16: Joshua conquered the whole land, including the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowlands, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its lowlands,
NET.17: from Mount Halak on up to Seir, as far as Baal Gad in the Lebanon Valley below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and executed them.
NET.18: Joshua campaigned against these kings for quite some time.
NET.19: No city made peace with the Israelites (except the Hivites living in Gibeon); they had to conquer all of them,
NET.20: for the LORD determined to make them obstinate so they would attack Israel. He wanted Israel to annihilate them without mercy, as he had instructed Moses.
NET.21: At that time Joshua attacked and eliminated the Anakites from the hill country — from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and all the hill country of Judah and Israel. Joshua annihilated them and their cities.
NET.22: No Anakites were left in Israelite territory, though some remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
NET.23: Joshua conquered the whole land, just as the LORD had promised Moses, and he assigned Israel their tribal portions. Then the land was free of war.
